mandates.name: Victorian Border Crossing Permit Directions
mandates.compliance: Must not enter Victoria
mandates.exemptions:
A prohibited person must not enter Victoria unless the prohibited person:
(a) is an aircrew services worker who is permitted to enter Victoria under clause 9; or
(b) has a valid transit permit under clause 10; or
(c) has a valid specified worker (other) permit under clause 11(1); or
(d) has a valid specified worker (exclusive outdoor activities) permit under clause 11(2); or
(e) has a valid specified worker (low workplace interaction) permit under clause 11(7); or
(f) is an excepted person under clause 13; or
(g) has a valid exemption under clause 3(5) or 14.
mandates.enforcement_measures:
A person who fails to comply with these directions is liable for an on-the-spot fine of:
i. aged 18 years or older – $1,652; aged 15 years or older but under the age of 18 years – $660.80; aged under 15 years – $165.20; or
in the case of a body corporate – $9,913; or
Refusing or failing to comply with a requirement to self-isolate or self-quarantine:
i. aged 18 years or older – $4,957; ii. aged 15 years or older but under the age of 18 years – $826.10; or
iii. under the age of 15 years – $165.20; 
Refusing or failing to comply with a requirement in relation to a person travelling from a restricted area (however described) and seeking to enter Victoria without a reasonable excuse or other valid reason or excuse, in the case of a natural person:
i. aged 18 years or older – $4,957; ii. aged 15 years or older but under the age of 18 years – $826.10; iii. under the age of 15 years – $165.20.
A person must not refuse or fail to comply with a direction given to the person, or a requirement made of the person, in the exercise of a power under an authorisation given under section 199.
In the case of a natural person, 120 penalty units; In the case of a body corporate, 600 penalty units.
Giving false and misleading information to an authorised officer. In the case of a natural person, 60 penalty units;In the case of a body corporate, 300 penalty units.

mandates.target: Quarantine Workers
mandates.compliance:
Must have at least one dose of the COVID vaccine by 25/06/21
By 01/09/21, the person has received 2 doses of a COVID-19 vaccine, or
(b) the person has received 1 dose of a COVID-19 vaccine and receives the second dose of a COVID-19 vaccine—

The Public Health Regulation 2012 also enables authorised officers to issue penalty notices for offences against clause 6 by individuals for an amount of $4,000 and $1,000 in other cases.

mandates.name: Queensland Health Residential Aged Care Facilities (COVID-19 Vaccination) Direction
mandates.target: health service employees in Queensland Health residential aged care facilities
mandates.compliance:
First dose by 16/09/21
Second dose by 31/10/21
Must show evidence of the first dose by 17/09/21 and second dose by 01/11/21
mandates.exemptions:
A health service employee who is unable to be vaccinated due to a medical contraindication or shortage of vaccinations may continue to work in a Hospital and Health Service or the Department of Health but must not enter, work in, or provide services in a Queensland Health residential aged care facility.
May enter if the entry, work or services are immediately necessary to provide emergency care to a resident of the facility.
May enter as a personal visitor of a resident of the facility or as a support person for a prospective resident, but must not enter, work in, or provide services as a health service employee, and must comply with all other public health directions applicable to entering a residential aged care facility.
Queensland Chief Health Officer, Deputy Chief Health Officer or delegate may grant an exemption (with or without conditions) to an operator or health service employee or class of employees or operators to respond to a critical workforce shortage. Or if an exemption is appropriate due to:
compassionate grounds or exceptional circumstances; or
the proportion of residents and employees at a facility that are vaccinated.
mandates.enforcement_measures:
Failure to comply with public health directions
A person to whom a public health direction applies must comply with the direction unless the person has a reasonable excuse.
Maximum penalty–100 penalty units or 6 months imprisonment.

mandates.name: COVID-19 Mandatory Vaccination and Vaccination Program Policy Version 2
mandates.target: WA health system entities and employees in a Residential aged care facility
mandates.compliance:
First dose by 17 September 2021
Fully vaccinated by 17 November 2021
mandates.exemptions:
1. a permanent medical exemption authorised by a medical practitioner
2. a temporary medical exemption authorised by a medical practitioner
3. an authorised temporary exemption or exception due to the inability to access a
COVID-19 vaccine
4. an authorised temporary exemption or exception due to a critical workforce
shortage, to maintain the provision of quality of care or to protect the health and
safety of residents, or
5. an authorised exemption or exception related to another category in the relevant
state or territory public health order.
mandates.enforcement_measures:
Unvaccinated Employees will initially be allowed to remain away from the workplace for a period
of two weeks without disciplinary action being commenced – the Preliminary Access Restriction
Period (PARP). The PARP provides time for the Employee to make a decision regarding their
intention to be Vaccinated and/or to receive a COVID-19 vaccine, prior to commencement of
formal disciplinary proceedings. The PARP will be unpaid.
Following the expiration of the two week PARP, the Employer may initiate disciplinary proceedings
in accordance with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Any decision to initiate disciplinary action, and subsequent disciplinary outcomes, will be
considered on a case by case basis and compliant with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Given the access restrictions provided for by the Aged Care Worker Directions, termination of
employment is a potential outcome for instances of non-compliance.
It is an offence for a person to fail, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any of these directions, punishable by a fine of up to $20,000 for individuals and $100,000 for bodies corporate.

mandates.compliance:
a person whose place of residence is in a declared area must not enter or remain on a construction site in Greater Sydney unless the resident—
(a) has had 2 doses of a COVID-19 vaccine, or
(b) has had 1 dose of a COVID-19 vaccine at least 21 days ago, or
(c) has had 1 dose of a COVID-19 vaccine within the preceding 21 days and has been tested for COVID-19 within the preceding 72 hours, or

A person must carry the required evidence, and produce the required evidence for inspection if requested.

has a certified medical contraindication

Corporations that fail to comply with a direction are liable to a fine of $55,000 and $27,500 each day the offence continues. The Public Health Regulation 2012 also enables authorised officers to issue penalty notices for offences against clause 6 by individuals for an amount of $4,000 and $1,000 in other cases.

mandates.target: Residential aged care facility workers
mandates.compliance:
Must be sufficiently vaccinated by 17/09/21 and provide proof
A person is sufficiently vaccinated if they have received all of the doses of a vaccine for the disease that is necessary for the person to be issued with a vaccination certificate issued by the Australian Immunisation Register
or received at least one dose of a vaccine for the disease and has made a booking to receive, as soon as is reasonably possible, all other required doses
or they have made a booking to receive the first dose of a vaccine for the disease as soon as is reasonably possible, provide evidence of the booking and will receive all the doses
mandates.exemptions:
(i) the person -
(A) is unable to be vaccinated against the disease due to a medical contraindication; and
(B) holds a medical certificate that certifies that; and
(C) provides a copy of that document the operator of the residential aged care facility that employs or engages the person or where the person is undertaking a clinical placement or work experience; or
(ii) the person -(A) is ineligible, due to the person's age, to be vaccinated against the disease until a later phase ofthe vaccination program (B) and provides the operator with evidence as to the age of the person;and
(iii) the person is an emergency management worker, who is only present to respond to an emergency (added in Direction no.2)
mandates.enforcement_measures:
The operator of a residential aged care facility must take all reasonable steps to -
(i) as soon as is practicable after this direction commences, notify each
person of the obligation on the person to be sufficiently vaccinated by 17 September 2021; and
(ii) on and after 17 September 2021, ensure that a person does not enter,or remain on,the premises of thefacility if the operator is not satisfied that the person - (A) is sufficiently vaccinated; or(e)(B) holds an exemption;
the operator of a residential aged care facility must ensure that -
(i) a copy of each of the following documents is kept and maintained by the facility: (A) each document provided to the operator as evidence of an exemption;
(B) each document provided to the operator as evidence of the vaccination status are provided to the Director of Public hlealth or his or her delegate as soon as possible after the request has been made

mandates.name: Mandatory Vaccination of Certain Workers No.2 to No.11
mandates.target: Quarantine site workers
mandates.compliance:
Must be fully vaccinated by 17/09/21 to enter the quarantine site
Must carry evidence of the person's vaccination status
A person is sufficiently vaccinated if they have received all of the doses of a vaccine for the disease that is necessary for the person to be issued with a vaccination certificate issued by the Australian Immunisation Register
or received at least one dose of a vaccine for the disease and has made a booking to receive, as soon as is reasonably possible, all other required doses
or they have made a booking to receive the first dose of a vaccine for the disease as soon as is reasonably possible, provide evidence of the booking and will receive all the doses
mandates.exemptions:
other than persons who are only present on the site for as long as is necessary to deliver goods to, or collect goods from, the site
(i) the person -
(A) is unable to be vaccinated against the disease due to a medical contraindication; and
(B) holds a medical certificate that certifies that; and
(C) provides a copy of that document to the relevant supevisor; or
(ii) the person -(A) is ineligible, due to the person's age, to be vaccinated until a later phase ofthe vaccination program (B) and provides the supevisor with evidence as to the age of the person;and
(iii) the person is an emergency management worker, who is only present to respond to an emergency
mandates.enforcement_measures:
A relevant supevisor must take all reasonable steps to 
(i) as soon as is practicable after this direction commences, notify each
person of the obligation on the person to be sufficiently vaccinated by 17 September 2021; and
(ii) on and after 17 September 2021, ensure that a person does not enter,or remain on,the premises of thefacility if the supevisor is not satisfied that the person - (A) is sufficiently vaccinated; or(e)(B) holds an exemption;
the relevant supevisor must ensure that -
(i) a copy of each of the following documents is kept and maintained by the facility: (A) each document provided to the operator as evidence of an exemption;
(B) each document provided to the operator as evidence of the vaccination status are provided to the Director of Public hlealth or his or her delegate as soon as possible after the request has been made
If a person does not follow the emergency orders, they may be issued a summons to go to Court. If convicted for breaching emergency orders, they can be fined up to $16,800 or be sentenced to prison for up to six months, or both.

mandates.name: Mandatory Vaccination of Certain Workers No.3 and onwards
mandates.target:
Medical or health facility workers
Medical service or treatment providers
Department of Health workers
mandates.compliance:
on and from 31 October 2021, a person is not permitted to provide health and medical services or treatments, work at medical or health facilities or work at the Department of Health unless the person is sufficiently vaccinated
Must carry evidence of vaccination status
A person is sufficiently vaccinated if they have received all of the doses of a vaccine for the disease that is necessary for the person to be issued with a vaccination certificate issued by the Australian Immunisation Register
or received at least one dose of a vaccine for the disease and has made a booking to receive, as soon as is reasonably possible, all other required doses
or they have made a booking to receive the first dose of a vaccine for the disease as soon as is reasonably possible, provide evidence of the booking and will receive all the doses
mandates.exemptions:
the person -
(i) providing health and medical services or treatments, in an
emergency circumstance, other than as part of their
employment or engagement; or
(ii) being engaged to provide services at a medical or health facility, other than health and medical services or treatments, in response to an emergency at the facility;and
(i) the person -
(A) is unable to be vaccinated against the disease due to a medical contraindication; and
(B) holds a medical certificate that certifies that; and
(C) provides a copy of that document to the relevant supevisor; or
(ii) the person -(A) is ineligible, due to the person's age, to be vaccinated until a later phase ofthe vaccination program (B) and provides the supevisor with evidence as to the age of the person;and
(iii) the person holds an exemption or is a member of a class of persons specified in an exemption
(iV) the person is an emergency management worker, who is only present to respond to an emergency
mandates.enforcement_measures:
the relevant supervisor must take all reasonable steps to -
(i) as soon as is practicable after this direction commences, notify the person that the person is required to be sufficiently vaccinated by 31 October 2021 and (ii) on and after 31 October 2021, ensure that the person does not enter, or remain on, the relevant location for the person if the relevant supervisor is not satisfied that the person -
(A) is sufficiently vaccinated against the disease as specified in paragraph (f); or
(B) is not required, under paragraph (g), to be sufficiently vaccinated againstthe disease; and
the relevant supevisor must ensure that -
(i) a copy of each of the following documents is kept and maintained by the facility: (A) each document provided to the operator as evidence of an exemption;
(B) each document provided to the operator as evidence of the vaccination status are provided to the Director of Public hlealth or his or her delegate as soon as possible after the request has been made

mandates.target: Health care worker - Tier 1 health care facilities
mandates.compliance:
·       First dose by 1 October 2021
·       Fully vaccinated by 1 November 2021
evidence in the form approved by the Chief Health Officer that they have
been vaccinated against COVID-19, if:
(a) directed to do so by an emergency officer; or
(b) required to do so by their employer or by the owner, occupier or person
apparently in charge of a health care facility.
mandates.exemptions:
defined under the Directions
Medical exemption, or a Temporary exemption approved by the Chief Health Officer or their delegate, or as otherwise outlined in the Directions. Or if they are:
(a) performing a law enforcement function that cannot reasonably be performed
other than by entering the health care facility; or
(b) performing a statutory duty that cannot reasonably be performed other than by entering the health care
facility; or
(c) performing any function or duty or exercising any right or power under a Fair
Work entry permit; or
(d) responding to an emergency in a capacity other than as a health care worker or
a health support worker; or
(e) providing emergency care to a patient in the health care facility where the
emergency care is necessary to be provided immediately and a fully vaccinated
or a partially vaccinated health care worker or health support worker is not available to provide that emergency care
Or an ad hoc volunteer
mandates.enforcement_measures:
Unvaccinated Employees will initially be allowed to remain away from the workplace for a period
of two weeks without disciplinary action being commenced – the Preliminary Access Restriction
Period (PARP). The PARP provides time for the Employee to make a decision regarding their
intention to be Vaccinated and/or to receive a COVID-19 vaccine, prior to commencement of
formal disciplinary proceedings. The PARP will be unpaid.
Following the expiration of the two week PARP, the Employer may initiate disciplinary proceedings
in accordance with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Any decision to initiate disciplinary action, and subsequent disciplinary outcomes, will be considered on a case by case basis and compliant with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Given the access restrictions provided for by the Aged Care Worker Directions, termination of
employment is a potential outcome for instances of non-compliance.
It is an offence for a person to fail, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any of these
directions, punishable by a fine of up to $20,000 for individuals and $100,000 for bodies
corporate.

The Public Health Regulation 2012 also enables authorised officers to issue penalty notices for offences against clause 6 by individuals for an amount of $4,000 and $1,000 in other cases.

mandates.name: COVID-19 Mandatory Vaccination (Workers) Directions
mandates.target: accommodation worker
mandates.compliance:
From 15/10/21, employees must provide vaccination information including bookings to receive doses
First dose by 22/10/21
Second dose by 26/11/21
mandates.exemptions:
if a worker has a booking to receive, by the first dose deadline, they are exempted
The exceptional circumstances are:
(a) a worker is required to perform work or duties that is or are necessary to provide for urgent specialist clinical or medical care due to an emergency situation or a critical unforeseen circumstance; or (b) a worker is required to fill a vacancy to provide urgent care, to maintain quality of care and/or to continue essential operations due to an emergency situation or a critical unforeseen circumstance; or a worker is required to respond to an emergency; or (d) a worker is required to perform urgent and essential work to protect
the health and safety of workers or members of the public, or to protect assets and infrastructure; or (e) an education worker that is required to: (i) carry out assessments of an oral or performance examination; or (ii) work as a venue coordinator for those examinations.
mandates.enforcement_measures:
A person must not refuse or fail to comply with a direction given to the person, or a requirement made of the person, in the exercise of a power under an authorisation given under section 199.
In the case of a natural person, 120 penalty units; In the case of a body corporate, 600 penalty units.
Giving false and misleading information to an authorised officer. In the case of a natural person, 60 penalty units;In the case of a body corporate, 300 penalty units.

mandates.name: Directions for mandatory vaccination of workers to attend the workplace
mandates.target:
(a) a worker who, during the course of work, is likely ot come into contact with a vulnerable person; (e.g. people working with children, disabled or elderly persons, health care, workers in Indigenous communities, retail services)
(b) a worker who is at risk of infection with COVID-19 because the worker, during the course of work, is likely to come into contact with a person or thing that poses a risk of infection; (e.g. health care workers in hospitals, police and emergency service workers, quaratine facilities, border control)
(c) a worker whose workplace poses a high risk of infection with COVID-19; (e.g. correction facilities, minign sites, food processing facilities, cruise vessels)
 (d) a worker who performs work that is necessary for the operation or maintenance of essential infrastructure or essential logistics in the Territory. (e.g. electricity, gas, water supply and sewerage treatment facilities, telecommunications systems and roads)
A comprehensive list is included in the directions

must provide evidence

a worker may attend the worker's workplace without being vaccinated with an approved COVID-19 vaccine fi the worker has evidence of a contraindication to all approved COVID-19 vaccines.

2021

may require a

doses of a COVID-19 vaccination.

has a COVID-19 vaccine exemption

provide an exemption from this Direction to:

mandates.enforcement_measures:
Unvaccinated Employees will initially be allowed to remain away from the workplace for a period
of two weeks without disciplinary action being commenced – the Preliminary Access Restriction
Period (PARP). The PARP provides time for the Employee to make a decision regarding their
intention to be Vaccinated and/or to receive a COVID-19 vaccine, prior to commencement of
formal disciplinary proceedings. The PARP will be unpaid.
Following the expiration of the two week PARP, the Employer may initiate disciplinary proceedings
in accordance with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Any decision to initiate disciplinary action, and subsequent disciplinary outcomes, will be considered on a case by case basis and compliant with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Given the access restrictions provided for by the Aged Care Worker Directions, termination of
employment is a potential outcome for instances of non-compliance.
It is an offence for a person to fail, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any of these
directions, punishable by a fine of up to $20,000 for individuals and $100,000 for bodies
corporate.

or received at least one dose of a vaccine for the disease and has made a booking to receive, as soon as is reasonably possible, all other required doses

mandates.target: Overseas flight crew members

NOT A MANDATE. Included to note that there is a difference between vaccinated and and unvaccinated arrivals
The flight crew member must go directly to the member’s place of residence or accommodation until the sooner of the following happens—

(iii) in an emergency situation,
Arrival by aircraft
(b) not permit another person to enter the place of residence or accommodation unless—
(i) the person usually lives at the place of residence or accommodation or the person is also complying with a direction under this Order, or

Section 10 of the Public Health Act 2010 creates an offence if an individual fails to comply with a direction with a maximum penalty of imprisonment for 6 months or a fine of up to $11,000 (or both) plus a further $5,500 fine each day the offence continues. Corporations that fail to comply with a direction are liable to a fine of $55,000 and $27,500 each day the offence continues. The Public Health Regulation 2012 also enables authorised officers to issue penalty notices for offences against clause 6 by individuals for an amount of $4,000 and $1,000 in other cases.

mandates.exemptions:
An exemption to the requirements in 5.1 of the policy may be available for workers who are unable to be vaccinated due to a medical contraindication to the any (sic) TGA approved and available COVID-19 vaccines. mandates.name: Directions for lock in areas
mandates.target: People in lock in areas
mandates.compliance: A person must not exit a lock-in area
mandates.exemptions:
Official Duties:
- Authorised officers.
- Persons performing functions under the Act or the Notifiable Diseases Act 1981.
- Essential workers who are vaccinated or have a contraindication to vaccination.
- Freight workers.
Medical and Health-related Reasons:
- Infected individuals needing to isolate.
- Persons suspected of having COVID-19 needing testing or assessment.
- Persons receiving medical treatment, testing, or vaccination related to COVID-19.
Legal and Administrative Purposes:
- Persons required to leave by law.
- Persons involved in justice system activities (e.g., attending court, police stations).
Essential Services:
- Obtaining goods or services from essential workers.
- Depositing waste when there's no local waste collection service.
Personal and Family Support:
- Providing care or support to family members or others unable to care for themselves.
- Childcare and education-related activities (dropping off/collecting children, attending school).
- Parents or guardians taking children to other parents or guardians.
Check directions for more detail
4/03/22 - added "An Aboriginal person who leads or conducts cultural rituals or ceremonies is an essential worker for these Directions."

mandates.target: Maritime crew on commercial vessels
mandates.compliance: Crew members must be vaccinated and quarantine
mandates.exemptions:
A crew member who is not vaccinated or exempt may apply for an
exemption to enter the Territory if the crew member is any of the
following:
(a) a crew member who is entering the Territory to begin residence in
the Territory;
(b) a crew member escaping domestic violence;
(c) active Australian military personnel required to assist the Territory
or required to enter the Territory while performing their official
duties;
(d) a specialist coming to the Territory to provide services for the
continuity of industry or business and the maintenance of
competitive operations if:
(i) the specialist's skills are difficult to obtain in the Territory; and
(ii) the service must be provided without delay; and
(iii) the specialist must be physically present in the Territory to
provide the service;
(e) a crew member coming to the Territory for necessary maintenance
or repair of power, water, communications or other infrastructure
critical to the Territory;
(f) a crew member, other than an abattoir or meat packing worker,
coming to the Territory to provide urgent services that are critical
to ensure continuity of the agricultural industry;
(g) a crew member who needs to enter the Territory for a
compassionate purpose.

Must record vaccination details when entering the territory

Section 10 of the Public Health Act 2010 creates an offence if an individual fails to comply with a direction with a maximum penalty of imprisonment for 6 months or a fine of up to $11,000 (or both) plus a further $5,500 fine each day the offence continues. The Public Health Regulation 2012 also enables authorised officers to issue penalty notices for offences against clause 6 by individuals for an amount of $4,000 and $1,000 in other cases.

mandates.name: Additional vaccination requirements for workers in certain settings
mandates.target: Residential aged care facility workers
mandates.compliance:
Must be vaccinated by 1/4/22 with at least one booster dose
After 1/4/22, a person is considered vaccinated if they are not eligible, in accordance with the ATAGI recommendations, to receive a booster dose of the vaccine; or are eligible, in accordance with the ATAGI recommendations, to receive a booster dose of the vaccine and receives a booster dose within 4 weeks of becoming eligible
mandates.exemptions:
1. (A) unable to be vaccinated against the disease due to a medical contraindication and (B) holds a document that certifies it or (ii) a medical exemption;
2. the person -(A) is fully vaccinated in respect of the disease; and is ineligible to receive a booster dose of a vaccine for the
disease under the vaccination program recognised by the
Director of Public Health or his or her delegate; and
provides his or her relevant supervisor with evidence as to why the person is currently ineligible to receive the booster dose; and receives that booster dose within 4 weeks of the person becoming eligible to receive the booster dose; or 
3. the person -
(A) holds an exemption, or is a member of a class of persons specified in an exemption, from the requirement to be vaccinated against the disease; and
(B) provides a legible copy of the exemption to his or her relevant supervisor; or
4. the person is an emergency management worker who is only
present on the premises fo rthe purpose of responding to an emergency
mandates.enforcement_measures: If a person does not follow the emergency orders, they may be issued a summons to go to Court. If convicted for breaching emergency orders, they can be fined up to $16,800 or be sentenced to prison for up to six months, or both.
mandates.executive_orders: Public Health Act 1997 DIRECTION UNDER SECTION 16 (Additional vaccination requirements for workers in certain settings- No.1)
mandates.removal_method: End of Public Health Emergency which removed all Public Health Directions made under the Emergency Declaration

(a) the worker has received at least 3 doses of an approved COVID-19 vaccine; or

mandates.exemptions:
(a) the worker was unable to receive the 3rd dose of an approved COVID-19 vaccine within 16 weeks of receiving the 2nd dose of an approved COVID-19 vaccine because the worker was infected with COVID-19 or was in quarantine; and

mandates.name: SS 7.1.9 COVID-19 Vaccination
mandates.target:
All NSW Rural Fire Service staff, volunteers and external labour (contractors) located at NSW RFS sites and working in close
proximity to members.
mandates.compliance:
at least two doses of a COVID-19 vaccine approved by the
Therapeutic Goods Administration for use in Australia.
Members are required to report their vaccination status and ensure it is recorded in their membership record. (For more details check the document NSW RFS COVID-19 RISK MANAGEMENT:
VACCINATION AND STATUS REPORTING)
mandates.exemptions:
The RFS will continue to consider and apply exemptions to mandatory vaccination in accordance with our existing policy position, as follows:

Medical exemption – a temporary exemption may be available for members who are unable to be vaccinated due to medical contraindication(s).
Junior member exemption – Junior volunteer members are not required to be vaccinated against COVID-19, but are strongly encouraged to follow ATAGI recommendations.
Brigade exemption – Districts continue to work with the 424 brigades who told us they were not supportive of mandatory vaccination as it would significantly impact their ability to provide fire and emergency service to their communities. Exemptions will be considered and determined for these brigades by no later than 30 June 2022.
mandates.enforcement_measures:
Where a staff member is found to be not complying with COVID-19 vaccination requirements in
this policy, the staff member will be instructed to take leave immediately. Staff may access
accrued recreation leave, extended leave, agreed absences (if eligible), and leave without pay, or
a combination of these types of leave for this purpose, but may not access sick leave or special
leave provisions.
5.2 If a medical exemption is accepted, an individual risk assessment will be performed to determine
if the staff member can continue in employment with additional control measures in place. Where
a workplace adjustment is required and cannot be made, consideration may be given to whether
the person can continue in employment.
5.3 If no exemption is granted it may be determined that the staff member has refused to comply with
a reasonable direction of the NSW RFS. Failure to comply with this reasonable direction may be
deemed a breach of the Service Standard 1.1.7 NSW RFS Code of Conduct and Ethics, may
result in misconduct action being undertaken in accordance with Section 69 of the Government
Sector Employment Act 2013, and may lead to termination of employment.

notableEvents.title: Delta becomes dominant variant
notableEvents.description: Delta variant becomes the dominant COVID-19 strain circulating in Australia, driving a significant increase in case numbers and prompting stricter mandate responses across multiple jurisdictions.

notableEvents.title: Extended lockdowns end in ACT, NSW and VIC
notableEvents.description: Following extended Delta-driven lockdowns, ACT, NSW, and Victoria lift stay-at-home orders as vaccination targets are reached, transitioning to living-with-COVID frameworks.

notableEvents.title: ATAGI recommends booster dose for high-risk populations
notableEvents.description: The Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (ATAGI) recommends a booster dose of COVID-19 vaccine for high-risk populations including aged care residents, healthcare workers, and the immunocompromised.

notableEvents.title: Omicron begins spreading across Australia
notableEvents.description: The Omicron variant is detected and begins spreading across Australian states, triggering renewed concern and prompting several jurisdictions to reimpose or extend mandate coverage.

notableEvents.title: WA hard border removed for fully vaccinated travellers
notableEvents.description: Western Australia removes its hard border, allowing fully vaccinated interstate and international travellers to enter without quarantine requirements, ending one of the last remaining state border closures in Australia.
